applies_to: PRO380-Eichrecht direct-connected 3x230/400 V, 40 A meter (MID + German MessEV calibration law, for EV chargers), user manual version 1.45, September 2025.
summary: The PRO380-Eichrecht is inepro's German calibration-law (Eichrecht) version of the PRO380, built into AC EV chargers. It has two RS485 Modbus RTU ports: RS485-1 for full access and RS485-2 as a read-only secondary. All registers are holding registers at hex addresses; live values are FLOAT32 in V, A, W, var and VA, and energy counters are INT32 in Wh by default. This map has its own register set and differs from the PRO380-Mod map.

addressing.note: The map is headed 'Holding register address (hex)'. The hex value goes on the wire unchanged, so 0x5012 (total active power) is decimal 20498, read with function 03.

source.title: PRO380-Eichrecht electricity meter - Full user manual EN
source.pages: RS485 spec section 4.5; terminals section 4.7; register map section 9.1 (pp. 18-24); error codes section 9.2 (p. 24); configurator energy data type and combination code (pp. 26-27)

notes: Energy data type (configurator section): default INT32, big-endian 32-bit integers in 1 Wh units over two holding registers; the alternative FLOAT32 is 'float ABCD' in kWh. Switch with 4026h (0 = FLOAT32, 1 = INT32). The energy rows here assume the default INT32.
Word order for the FLOAT32 live values is taken from the manual's description of its FLOAT32 type as 'float ABCD' (high word first).
The map prints the unit 'var' for reactive energy counters 6024h-6046h; they are energy counters and are listed here as varh, as on the quadrant rows (6063h on).

Left out: serial number and product id (packed BCD), meter code (marked TODO in the manual), phase direction (ASCII), CT ratio and S0 output rate (marked not used), checksums and active status word, LCD custom fields, the waveform sample buffer (47FDh-4800h) and the blocking 'update wait' register 4081h.
Two power-peak registers (5064h and 5066h) are both named 'Previous Forward Active Power Peak' in the source; 5066h is most likely the reverse one, but the name is copied as printed.
The RS485 spec lists baud rates 1200-115200, address range 0-247 and up to 31 meters per bus.

registers.name: Combination code
registers.description: How forward and reverse energy are combined into the total counters.

registers.name: LCD cycle time
registers.description: Minimum display time per LCD message (default 3 s).

registers.name: Error code
registers.description: Error bitfield; also shown on the LCD.

registers.name: Power on/off counter
registers.description: Power cycle count; write 0 to clear.

registers.name: Peak power interval
registers.description: Peak detection interval in minutes; 0 = off, 1-60 (default 15).

registers.name: Resettable day counter
registers.description: Write 0 to clear the day counter.

registers.name: Previous day counter
registers.description: Day counter value before the last clear.

integration.summary: Connect to RS485-1 (terminals 22/23), poll unit 1 at 9600 baud, even parity with function 03. Read live values as ABCD floats from 5000h and energy as big-endian INT32 Wh from 6000h.
integration.enable: No enable step is described. Settings (ID, baud, parity, energy data type, combination code) can be written over Modbus or with inepro's EichrechtMeterConfig tool.
quirks: Power is in W/var/VA here, unlike the PRO380-Mod which reports kW.
Energy is INT32 Wh by default; setting 4026h = 0 switches to FLOAT32 kWh, which keeps only about 6 significant digits.
Baud rate is written as a code (6 = 9600), not as the number.
setup: RS485-1 A/B on terminals 22/23 is the primary port; RS485-2 on 24/25 is read-only.
Defaults: Modbus ID 1, 9600 baud, even parity.
The optical port uses fixed settings: 4800 baud, even parity, ID 1.
gotchas: Forward and reverse counters are always positive; the combination code only affects the total counters, not power.

verified.method: independent re-check of every register against the source PDF
